findings.element: 'Import method' select inside the Integration source card (manual panel) vs the 'Use automatic retrieval' toggle above it
findings.finding: Picking 'Automated (recommended)' from the Integration card while the manual panel is open removes every upload block, disables 'Run reconciliation', and leaves the page in the manual panel with the toggle still reading 'Use automatic retrieval' — two controls set the same mode and disagree about which one is active, with nothing on screen to act on.
findings.user_impact: The user lands on a screen that says everything is automated yet refuses to run, with no upload block to fill and no cue that the recovery is to re-pick Manual or click the toggle, so they stall on a self-contradictory state.
findings.suggested_fix: Make the toggle and the per-card Import method selects read from one mode value so the panel, the toggle label and the card select always agree, and never allow a combination that yields zero actionable controls plus a disabled Run.

evidence.action: Opened the manual panel via 'Upload manually', then set the Integration card's Import method to 'Automated (recommended)' from inside that panel
evidence.observed: Upload blocks = 0, Run reconciliation disabled=true, automatic card still visible=false (page stays in the manual panel), toggle above still labelled 'Use automatic retrieval'

findings.finding: Whenever the run is blocked the button is simply set disabled with no tooltip, no inline list of what is missing and no visible change to the upload blocks, so nothing on screen names the precondition that failed.
findings.user_impact: Users who removed a file, or who switched to PayPal and lost the automatic option, see a dead primary button and no statement of what to fix — the exact generic-blocker dead end that KF-9 identifies as the top source of production friction.
findings.suggested_fix: Replace the silent disabled state with a named blocker next to the button — e.g. 'Add the General ledger export to continue' or 'PayPal has no automatic retrieval, so both files must be uploaded' — and highlight the specific block that is still empty.

evidence.action: Filled all three upload blocks (Run became enabled), then clicked 'Remove' on one chip; separately switched the Integration select from Stripe to PayPal
evidence.observed: Remove -> chips=2, Run disabled=true with no message naming what is now missing. PayPal -> automatic card hidden, 'Upload manually' toggle disappears (visible=false), Run disabled=true, and nothing on screen explains why the automatic option is gone

findings.element: 'Upload manually' / 'Use automatic retrieval' toggle in the 'How we get the data' section
findings.finding: Clicking back to automatic retrieval silently discards every file already picked, with no warning before and no notice after.
findings.user_impact: A user who uploads two or three exports, clicks the toggle to check what automatic retrieval would do, and clicks back loses all of that work with no indication it happened — and only discovers it when Run is disabled again with no blocker named.
findings.suggested_fix: Preserve picked files across mode switches, or warn before clearing them ('Switching to automatic retrieval will discard the 3 files you added').

evidence.action: In manual mode filled the upload blocks, clicked the toggle to 'Use automatic retrieval' (click 2), then clicked it again to return to manual (click 3)
evidence.observed: Click 2 -> automatic card visible=true, Run re-enabled, files already picked silently discarded; click 3 -> manual panel returns with the blocks empty and no message about the discarded files

findings.element: Setup form after clicking 'Run reconciliation' (status region '#running' plus the still-live Period / Integration / Account controls)
findings.finding: Once the run starts the whole form above stays enabled and editable even though edits no longer affect anything, and the status region never states what was actually submitted.
findings.user_impact: A user who notices a wrong period right after starting will change the date select, see it accept the new value, and believe the run now covers the corrected range when it does not — and there is no cancel and no summary anywhere to correct that belief.
findings.suggested_fix: On run, freeze the form and replace it with a read-only summary of exactly what was submitted (period, integration, account, data source), plus a cancel or 'change and re-run' action.

evidence.action: Clicked 'Run reconciliation' with automatic retrieval selected, then inspected the form above the status region
evidence.observed: Button became 'Running…'/disabled and #running showed 'Reconciliation started…', but the date select remained enabled=true and editable while changing it does nothing; no confirmation step, no summary of what is being compared, no way to cancel

findings.element: Custom start / end date inputs in the Period section
findings.finding: The custom range accepts an end date earlier than the start date and ranges entirely in the future, echoes the nonsense range back in the hint as if it were valid, and leaves 'Run reconciliation' enabled.
findings.user_impact: The user starts a long-running reconciliation (the copy warns it can take hours) over a range that cannot match anything, and only learns it was wrong when the result comes back empty — with no error on the page to point at the date.
findings.suggested_fix: Validate the range on change: block or auto-correct end-before-start, flag future-only ranges inline next to the inputs, and keep Run disabled until the range is valid.

evidence.action: With Custom selected, set the end date before the start date (2026-08-31 → 2026-08-01), then set an entirely future range (2027-01-01 to 2027-12-31)
evidence.observed: Hint rendered '2026-08-31 – 2026-08-01' and then '2027-01-01 – 2027-12-31', error element count on page = 0, Run reconciliation disabled=false in both cases

gaps: Upload blocks: the prototype fabricates a file on 'Browse' (no real input[type=file]), so wrong-file-type, oversized-file and parse-failure states were never reached — whether the upload path tells the user what went wrong is unknown, not passed.
No upload progress or parsing state exists after a file is added, so nothing was observed about how the user is told a file was accepted beyond the chip appearing.

Automatic-retrieval failure and empty-result states are not implemented, so the KF-9 precondition failures this flow most needs to surface (closed accounting period, lost QBO authorization, missing account mappings, multicurrency not enabled) could not be evaluated at all — the run only ever reports 'Reconciliation started'.

Close (✕): the state map records no visible change, no dialog and no navigation, so whether it actually discards a filled-in setup — and therefore whether the missing confirmation is a real data-loss risk — could not be determined.
No results / matched-unmatched screen exists after Run, so nothing could be checked about how the outcome of the primary task is communicated.
